comments.text:
Corrected Gear ratio. Mistakenly input Dans Healey ratio versus this vehicle.
This vehicle has a 4.3 ratio rear end and a direct drive setup so the Final Drive ratio should be 4.3 unless incorrect information has been relayed to me.
Asked Ryan to gather Wifi credentials for this client.
Client stopped by today to drop off License plates. And provided the details at that time.
ID: ATT8072B
pw: h1aj2u123K
Devin uploaded this data to the vehicle.
Went through and verified heater operations.
Found that this vehicle has the heater circuit wired differently than our new standards.
Blower motor and heater contactor are trigged by the same switch using the same output from the PDU.
At this point in time upper management says that this should be fine since our older cars have been wired this way without any major issues.
The proper fix to this would be to move the contactor positive lead over to the "AC Blower" positive in the HVAC sub and have it commanded on based on the current level of the Heat Blower output from the pmu. This prevents the heater from turning on unless there is a load present on the heater blower motor.
However as the vehicle sits the heater is enabled and works as built.
Also Uploaded the current PMU Project files to the drive under the vehicle folder. That way this can be referenced in the future if necessary.If any PMU changes are made we will need to reupload or replace what was there.

comments.text: Reviewed my new torque based tune and tested in the vehicle. The boost is still quite noticeable even with a perfectly flat torque feedback. comments.text: Reviewed new Claude posts since yesterday. Reviewed trial notes. Repeated baseline current derate test and then tried a medium and max derate tune. In eco mode things are feeling way better but for some reason that changes switching back over to sport. Log analysis backs that up with current figures, derate sounding like more of a band aid solution now. Browsed all the various inverter feedback signals for any that seem to get rough at the same time. Noticed phase B current is always 0, turned out to be the DBC or something not important.

comments.author: Brandon Beaman
comments.text:
Date: Friday, September 18, 2026
Vehicle/System: Ritchie 71 Blazer — Ampere EV VCU (New Eagle VCM_519)
Firmware: DiagCANSW 1.8.13 / build 516 → 1.9.3 / build 519 (VCM_519_RC010903_Persist)
Status: VCU adjustments finalized
Objective
Flash Ritchie to the new 1.9.3 VCU firmware, identify every calibration the flash reset to factory defaults, restore the shop's drivability settings, and validate regen behavior on road.
What we did
Captured a full pre-flash screenshot set across all tabs, flashed to 1.9.3 / build 519, and captured a matching post-flash set. Ran a field-by-field pre/post comparison to find what did not carry over. Restored the affected calibrations with Marc's direction, then ran three instrumented test drives — a regen baseline, a BrkTrqReqTblHigh validation run, and a final AWD-enabled run — logging each to CSV. Backed up the inverter and PMU configurations to the Drive. Cross-referenced Ritchie's tables against Preheim's for a known-good reference. Closed out the remaining rate adjustment at end of day; VCU calibration is now final.
Key findings
Ten calibrations did not survive the flash. Everything else on the eight comparable tabs was identical. The losses cluster in two places — pedal/torque and high-regen braking:
Pedal and torque
APPTrqReqMapEco — full pedal was 50% torque, reset to 100%
APPTrqReqMap (Normal) — full pedal was 75% torque, reset to 100%
APPTrqReqMapSport — still 100% at top, but sharper off idle (20% pedal was 20% torque, now 30%)
Pedal axes (APP11IdxArr, …Eco, …Sport) — were even 10% steps, now 0/4/10/20/30/40/50/62.5/75/87.5/100
DrvTrqReqFiltTC 0.005 → 0.050 s
DrvTrqReqRateLimIncTbl 300 → 500 Nm/s at 0 kph; 2500 → 3000 Nm/s at 100 kph (~62 mph)
DrvTrqReqRateRateLimInc 25000 → 1500 Nm/s/s
Brake regen — Driver_RegenLevel reads High on this truck, so all four are live:
BrkTrqReqTblHigh was a flat −1.25 / −1.40 / −1.50 m/s² at every vehicle weight; now weight-tiered −0.30 to −1.10. Materially less braking regen.
VehSpd07IdxArrHigh first two breakpoints 0 / 2 kph → 5 / 12.5 kph (0 / 1.2 mph → 3.1 / 7.8 mph)
RegenTrqReqRateHighLimInc −100 → −50
RegenRateLimHighIncTbl −100 / −100 / −300 / −400 / −400 → flat −50
Drivability is now scaled, not per-table. 1.9.3 replaces the three separate pedal maps with a single table plus an Eco/Normal/Sport percentage. Per Marc, set back to 50 / 75 / 100.
A hidden torque limit was masking the regen fix. DrvMtrTrqLimMn_AEM_LDU_Sport sat at −400 pre-flash; we adjusted it to −300 before test driving. Marc confirmed the previously-fixed "800s" had a limit underneath that wasn't accounted for. Table re-adjusted.
The −50 rate was a red herring. On review, the RegenRateLimHighIncTbl −50 is a rate, not the cap — reset to −50 and moved on.
Restoring BrkTrqReqTblHigh changed feel, not magnitude. With the table set back to pre-flash values for the truck's current weight category (all other fields untouched), regen braking became noticeably more responsive but not any stronger. Logged as VCM_519_Motoring Diag_2026_09_18_01_56_27.csv.
A/C pressure protection carried over clean — including the bug. All fifteen fields identical pre to post: static and running high/low thresholds, all four time thresholds, sensor gain, offset and filter. ACPress_RunLow_Thr still reads −500 / −475 kPa. Since this flash overwrote ten other calibrations and left this one alone, −500 is Ampere's own default, not a shop entry — the same negative threshold seen on Lee's Mustang and on Preheim.
AWD tab restructured. BrkTrqReqTblAWD is new in 1.9.3 — Preheim doesn't have it (old firmware), so the −2.2 reference point it was compared against isn't real; Preheim's table reads −1.5, matching how Ritchie is set now. Andrew dropped the weight dimension entirely on the new AWD table; it's speed-based only, which is the same table we changed last time that moved DrvTrqReqRaw from −49 to −93.
Park brake / E-Stop: closed, no action. Wilwood actuator timings carried over unchanged. E-Stop entries are hardware this truck doesn't have.
Final calibration state
VCU adjustments on Ritchie are finalized as of end of day. The last change was the increase rate-rate setting (DrvTrqReqRateRateLimInc), adjusted and screenshotted at 4:42 PM after Marc's review of the AWD-enabled log. No further table changes are outstanding on this truck.
Test drives and logs

undefined
Truck is back on and uploading the AWD-enabled log.
Artifacts produced
Full pre-flash and post-flash screenshot sets, all tabs — attached to the ClickUp monthly goal

Preheim RDIS comparison (old vs. new) for reference
Three instrumented drive logs (above)
Status
Flash complete and stable. All ten reset calibrations identified and addressed; drivability, torque-limit, and regen rate settings restored and validated on road. VCU adjustments finalized — no open changes on this truck. Backups secured. Remaining work is display/logging additions and the Ampere threshold item, none of which block the vehicle.



Spent quite a bit of time today pretty much all day getting through checkout on this vehicle.
Most of the time spent today was testing and tuning the new VCU AWD firmware with Marc.
The EOD report above has a good summary of all the details.
Billy is taking the vehicle home this weekend to test everything.
Any issues needing to be resolved will be relayed to me ASAP.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Worked with Brandon to develop a better PMU revision system. Cleaned up the master branch and backed up on google drive. Had Brandon pull this down and showed him how to flash to the PMU's along with a number of other vehicle startup details to follow along first. Moved on to the VCU, showed Brandon about the firmware builds and Raptor structures. Converted vehicle requirements into a VCU config. Moved on to the inverter while Brandon loaded that. Upgraded the inverter firmware and flashed EEPROM in line with a W motor while following along in thee sheet.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Continued startup with Brandon and Dave. Hooked up HV and key'd on. Tried charging and got the ChgPortContFlt, verified all the associated wiring that has caused that fault previously, no problems found. Tried charging again and it just worked this time. Verified battery heater. Calibrated the resolver. Troubleshot cabin heater wiring. Searched and searched for documentation but couldn't find complete references. Experementially found the VCU was telling the PMU to tell the VCU to turn on the heat. Took thorough notes on actual wiring.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Verified K33 "Heat Request" functionality on Prehiem to make sure I had the correct tags in Raptor-Service. Tried various combinations of PMU outputs and VCU configs to determine if there was a way to get powering up the heater logic unit as the mechanism to enable heat. Ends up with a fault in the VCU which makes adding a relay the easier option. Drew a diagram for and wired up a relay to a spare output on the PMU. Wrote logic to check the temp knob below 15%, the fan knob above 30%, as well as negative contactor and ignition on. Tested all knob positions and GUI inputs while watching in Raptor and the PMU software. The GUI indicates correctly and warm air blows. I never let it heat up enough to judge effectiveness. Only thing left for HVAC now is to charge the AC and tune that in.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Verified heater circuit actually working by monitoring CAN data from the heater itself for output power. Double checked with a second data source Pack_Current from the BMS. Modified the PMU logic to also include fan and temp knobs as a criteria for turning on the cabin heat pump. Tested all scenarious with the user inputs from the GUI and knobs. Noticed the battery pump was running when it usually isn't, started to investigate, met for various discussions with the team before I could finish. Plugged into Preheim to investigate source of the difference in control.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Tuned in the AC compressor with Dave, it's working as expected plus a little 'bonus'. The AC compressor 'hiccups' with HV connected but the logic unit powered off. Powering up the compressor logic controller without Ampere commanding it to actually compress causes a VCU level fault. Shared to Slack.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Catching up on Slack before the meeting. Looked into Claudes diagnosis of the AC issue. Looks like the PMU program has never changed for that channel and Claude picked up on the troubleshooting I did as the actual problem, not knowing that at time the system was supposed to be operating different than the rest of the fleet. This was required to verify the 450V compressor functions differently than the 400V one and would work better under a different control sequence. Verified VCU settings for the battery were wrong and corrected.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Forced the car to suck out the BMS config again and the fully charged range estimate dropped from 306.04 to 149.58 miles. The new battery health calculations result in 146.4 Ah for the pack, a very reasonable estimate. Also verified Dave's findings on the AC compressor from the computer side. The hiccup issue has been magically fixed.

comments.text:
Went through the VCU and verified all of the Vehicle Parameters were set into the VCU appropriately.
The tire size on this vehicle is 185vR15... there isnt any aspect ratio listed. According to the googles though total diameter is approx 675mm to 677mm.
Adjusted settings appropriately in the VCU and  switched all of the parameters from Display to Calibration.
Test drove the vehicle with Dave. Found that the GUI displayed the same speed as my Phone did. Speedo gauge was approx 1-2mph high.
Adjusted tire size down from 0.675 to 0.665.
Vehicle can be test driven again to verify that we are closer to a 0 delta. Not 100% sure if there is a filter that Peterson is adding to the speed or not but that would explain the slight difference. Or the fact that the GUI and My phone were both using GPS data while the speedo gauge was using calculations. Either way we are much much closer than the 20% that was noticed
Final vehicle weight wasn't recorded explicitly so the weight that is in there is close but not exact.
Messaged Ryan to gather the wifi credentials for this car.

comments.author: Brandon Beaman
comments.text:
Noticed the GUI in this vehicle is operating a tad bit different than other GUIs we have had in the past.
Went through the Update process for the GUI.
Updated and or Installed all necessary .apk files.
Updated .xml file and realdash dashboard.
Operations found to boot at different speeds.
The boot time on this GUI is much much faster than all of our other units. Unsure why this is at this time.
Ampere Software will finish booting before CAN 3 messages are ready.
So there is a slight " loading time " feel present for this vehicle. This however seems to be normal operation on all our vehicles except boot times are a bit longer so by the time everything loads the Messages are already there and present so there isnt that "loading" feeling.
Possible we take a trace of CAN3 and have claude see if there are any noticeable issues with it.

Verified Teague was on the VCU firmware that we talked about this morning. Sat in the car with the vehicle on.
Found that the AC was acting as intended. No noticeable hiccups or blips from the AC compressor.
So as of right now Yes the fix in the VCU_516_Beta10813_SDU_Persist should be moved over to the newest firmware to allow us to update this vehicle and keep the Hiccup fix.
However this car is still experiencing the AC low voltage errors.
As the car is turning off you can observe the HV Fault lamp pop up on the right before the GUI screen turns off. So this seems like its happening during Key Off. Maybe we have Andrew look into the thresholds that may be causing this as well. Has the contactors open but the CAN messages are still sending Valid checks?
